title: Make our store agent-ready and price-resilient as PC costs climb
summary: 55% of consumers use AI in product discovery (NIQ); Walmart added agent profiles and spending limits, Amazon widened Shop Direct. PC shipments fell 21% in Q3 (Counterpoint); Asus sees commercial PC prices up ~10% in 2H26.

points.headline: Retailers are setting the rules for AI shopping agents
points.detail: Walmart added agent profiles, terms and spending limits; Amazon expanded Shop Direct. We should decide how agents may read and buy from our store.

points.headline: AI is now a mainstream discovery channel for shoppers
points.detail: NIQ finds 55% of consumers use AI in discovery; Gartner says 34% of US shoppers would use GenAI for gift ideas. Our product content must work for AI tools.

points.headline: PC demand is falling while component costs push prices up
points.detail: Counterpoint: Q3 shipments down 21%, Q4 decline forecast at 27%. Asus expects commercial prices up ~10% in 2H26. We should plan promotions, pricing and inventory.

points.headline: IDC: memory-shortage fears raise PC buyers’ interest in financing
points.detail: With costs rising, business buyers look to flexible financing. We should test leasing and instalment offers for business buyers in our store.

points.headline: Walmart stretches Black Friday and Cyber Monday to 14 days
points.detail: Walmart extended its events from 10 to 14 days, which may pull electronics demand earlier. We should check our deal calendar and price matching.
